intro: Madagascar split from India about 88 million years ago, and most of its plants and animals evolved in isolation.

chapters.title: Unique wildlife
text: All wild lemurs live only in Madagascar, along with fossas, chameleons and baobab trees. About 90% of its wildlife is found nowhere else.

chapters.title: Land
text: Highlands run down the middle; the east has rainforest, the west dry forest and the 'Avenue of the Baobabs', and the south spiny forest. The Tsingy are forests of razor-sharp limestone.

keyTerms.meaning: A primate found only in Madagascar.

places.title: Landscape tour
places.intro: Places that show the variety of Madagascar's landscapes. The numbers match the pins on the map.
